Headline

1. The procedure file is written, and all three notes files now pass the checks.
2. I wrote `notes/procedure.md` with six numbered steps that use `check_file`, `read_file`, and `write_file`.
3. I applied the procedure to `notes/a.md`, `notes/b.md`, and `notes/c.md` in that order.
4. A final `check_file` run on each file reports no banned words and no long sentences.

Background

The request asked for a reusable fix procedure, written first, then applied to three notes files. Each file had style failures reported by the deterministic checker.

Relevance

The procedure is generic, so any agent can apply it to any notes file. The three files now meet the style rules while keeping their meaning.

Information

The fixes per file, based on the checker output:

| File | Failure found | Fix applied |
|---|---|---|
| a.md | Banned word "clearly" | Removed it without changing the speed claim [inference: the sentence makes the same claim without the booster] |
| b.md | One sentence over 25 words | Split into three sentences, order of events kept |
| c.md | Banned word "very", one sentence over 25 words | Removed "very", split the long sentence into four |

Final check results: all four files report zero banned words and zero sentences over 25 words (checker output, this session).

Alternative considered: rewriting the sentences with different words instead of splitting. It loses because splitting preserves the original wording and order most closely.

End

I recommend that we:

1. Keep `notes/procedure.md` as the standard fix procedure. Domain: Clear, because the checker gives a deterministic pass or fail, so best practice applies. Test (deterministic):
   Given `notes/procedure.md` exists,
   When `check_file` runs on it,
   Then it reports no failures.
2. Use the procedure for any new notes file before commit. This removes the blocker of repeated manual edits. Domain: Clear, with the same reasoning. Test (deterministic):
   Given a notes file under `notes/`,
   When an agent applies steps 1 to 6 of the procedure,
   Then `check_file` reports no failures.
3. Re-run `check_file` on all notes files after any edit. Domain: Clear, one known step. Test (deterministic):
   Given a modified notes file,
   When `check_file` runs after the edit,
   Then it reports no failures.

Follow-up

No open questions. The fixes in a.md and c.md depend on judgment calls (removing boosters), labeled [inference] where meaning was at stake; the split edits in b.md and c.md preserve wording.

arguments.content:
# Procedure: fix banned words and long sentences in a notes file

1. Run `check_file` on the target file with the tools. Note each banned word and each sentence over 25 words.
2. Read the file with `read_file` to get the full text.
3. For each banned word, remove it or replace it. Keep the meaning of the sentence.
4. For each sentence over 25 words, split it into two or more sentences. Keep the meaning and the order of ideas.
5. Write the fixed text with `write_file`. Replace the whole file.
6. Run `check_file` again. If it still reports problems, repeat steps 3 to 5 until the file is clean.

# Release note

The new parser is faster than the old one. It reads a large log in two seconds.

# Incident note

The outage started when the cache filled up during the nightly import. The service fell back to the database for every request. This continued until the import job ended an hour later.

# Design note

The queue is simple. Each worker takes one message. It runs the job. It writes the result to the store. Then it marks the message as done, so no other worker picks it up again.
